title: Nonstationary finite-armed bandits: known variance and variation budgets.
summary: The learner knows the environment-wide variance and mean-variation budgets and receives one bounded reward from the selected arm each round. The target is dynamic pseudo-regret, allowing zero noise and zero variation. The variance budget sums, over time, the maximum variance among all arms in each round.

description_paragraphs: The learner knows the environment-wide variance and mean-variation budgets and receives one bounded reward from the selected arm each round. The target is dynamic pseudo-regret, allowing zero noise and zero variation. The variance budget sums, over time, the maximum variance among all arms in each round.

model.instance: The environment fixes reward laws $\nu_{t,i}$ supported on $[0,1]$, with means $\mu_{t,i}$ and variances $\sigma_{t,i}^2$. Rewards are independent across rounds and may be dependent across arms within a round. Public budgets Q,B satisfy $\sum_t\max_i\sigma_{t,i}^2\le Q$ and $\sum_{t=2}^T\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty\le B$.

assumptions.description: The budget is Σ_{t=1}^T max_i σ²_{t,i} ≤ Q. It is neither the sum of variances of selected arms nor the sum across all arms.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: The sum $\sum_{t=2}^T\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty$ has a public upper bound. It excludes the initial mean and is not sample-path variation.

model.parameter_domain_description: B: $0\le B\le T-1$ (public); K: $K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2$ (public); Q: $0\le Q\le T/4$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public)
interaction_timing: All reward marginals are fixed in advance. K, T, Q, and B are public.
Select $a_t$ using the history and private randomness.
A fresh reward from the current arm is returned; other arms' rewards are not revealed within that round.
model.adversary_information: Distributions or functions are fixed before interaction. A round’s fresh sample is drawn after the action and probes are chosen, independently of past history and the learner’s private randomness.
unresolved_applicability: The 2026 source model, budget convention, and statement have been checked. Full mathematical review of the calibrated/clipped upper bound and the independent lower bound remains incomplete, so those candidate claims are excluded from the accepted envelopes.

The source assumes T at least two, whereas the recorded parameter domain allows T at least one. This endpoint difference must be handled explicitly by regimes and coverage; the theorem is not assumed to include T=1.
model.independence: Rewards are independent across rounds. Potential rewards of different arms in one round may be correlated because only one is observed. After selecting the current arm, its conditional law remains the fixed distribution nu_{t,a_t}.
model.source_horizon_qualification: The original model in ON_SRC_NS26, Section 2, assumes T at least two. T=1 is a degenerate endpoint of the problem definition; the current candidate bounds are not thereby certified at that endpoint.
description_paragraphs: Nonstationary reward distributions $\nu_{t,i}$ are fixed in advance, supported on $[0,1]$, and independent across rounds. Potential rewards of unselected arms within a round need not be independent.
The public environment-variance budget $Q$ constrains $\sum_t\max_i\operatorname{Var}(X_{t,i})$, rather than summing variances only for arms actually selected by the learner.
The public total mean-variation budget $B$ excludes the initial mean vector. It is distinct from a variance budget or the number of best-arm switches.
Require $K\ge2$, $0\le Q\le T/4$, and $0\le B\le T-1$.
The problem is defined at $T=1$, but the source model and theorem start at $T\ge2$. Its conclusion therefore does not cover the one-round endpoint.
Assume $K,T\ge2$, $0\le Q\le T/4$, and $0\le B\le T-1$. The source all-budget theorem is stated only on these ranges. The case $T=1$ can be treated separately as a direct finite problem.

operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: The action is randomized before the current reward is revealed, so the current choice and conditional variance are predictable in the refined filtration. Only the selected arm is observed; arm means and variances are hidden. The budgets Q and B are public, but future mean and variance schedules are not.

operations.coupling: The action is randomized before the current reward is revealed, so the current choice and conditional variance are predictable in the refined filtration. operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and explicitly permitted probes. The environment controls the current loss, outcome, or fresh sample; the learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Follow the interaction order in registry.protocols exactly. Current loss feedback follows the action; any pre-action context or advice phase is specified separately.

auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.
description_paragraphs: The currently selected arm’s bounded random reward:

$$
t,\ a_t\in[K]\ \longmapsto\ Y_t\sim\nu_{t,a_t},\quad\mathbb{E}[Y_t\mid\mathcal{H}_{t-1},a_t]=\mu_{t,a_t},\quad\operatorname{Var}(Y_t\mid\mathcal{H}_{t-1},a_t)=\sigma_{t,a_t}^2
$$
The action is randomized before the current reward is revealed, making the choice and conditional variance predictable in the refined filtration.
Only one selected-arm sample is returned. Arm means and variances are hidden.
Only the budgets $Q,B$ are public; future mean and variance schedules are hidden.
Public inputs: K, T, variance-envelope budget Q, and mean-variation budget B.

output.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
description_paragraphs: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.

metric.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The compared mean losses or rewards lie in $[0,1]$, so cumulative pseudo-regret lies in $[0,T]$.
description_paragraphs:
$$
\sum_t\max_i\sigma_{t,i}^2\le Q,\quad\sum_{t=2}^T\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty\le B,\quad R_T=\sum_t(\max_i\mu_{t,i}-\mu_{t,a_t})
$$

algorithms.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
algorithms.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All measurable causal policies satisfying the declared information timing and feasible domain are allowed, without extra span, iteration-form, or polynomial-time restrictions.
algorithms.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real internal computation is allowed. The algorithm knows Q,B; adaptation to unknown budgets is not automatic. The 2026 upper bound uses calibration, screening, clipping, and restarts. Every actual pull counts toward T; internal processing gives no additional native feedback or arithmetic/bit guarantee.
algorithms.parallelism: Online rounds proceed sequentially. A two-point evaluation is a same-round feedback pair, not two independent rounds.
description_paragraphs: All measurable causal randomized policies respecting the stated timing are allowed. The private seed is independent of the fixed instance and future samples. Apart from explicit feedback, output, and budget requirements, there are no restrictions on linear spans, iteration form, internal arithmetic, memory, or communication.

guarantees.complete_expression: The native objective is $\inf_{\mathcal A(K,T,Q,B)}\sup_{(\nu_{t,i})\ \mathrm{obeying}\ Q,B}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A,\nu}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: Take the infimum over algorithms knowing only public K, T, and supplied budgets.
Take the supremum over admissible time-varying distribution schedules fixed before interaction.
The comparator is the deterministic largest mean $\mu_t^\star$ in each round, without switching costs.
Expectation covers learner randomness and the selected reward samples. The objective is cumulative mean gap, not comparison with the best realized reward trajectory in hindsight.
guarantees.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
guarantees.time_uniformity: The T-round horizon is fixed and public. No anytime or simultaneous-all-T high-probability guarantee is implied.
description_paragraphs:
$$
\inf_{\mathcal{A}(K,T,Q,B)}\sup_{(\nu_{t,i})\ \mathrm{obeying}\ Q,B}\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{A},\nu}[R_T]
$$

Choose one algorithm using public inputs before taking the worst case over all admissible instances. Expectation covers the algorithm's private randomness and the observation randomness specified by the model. Comparator choice and the order of summation, minimization, and expectation follow the displayed formula.

objects.definition: The environment fixes reward laws $\nu_{t,i}$ supported on $[0,1]$, with means $\mu_{t,i}$ and variances $\sigma_{t,i}^2$. Rewards are independent across rounds and may be dependent across arms within a round. Public budgets Q,B satisfy $\sum_t\max_i\sigma_{t,i}^2\le Q$ and $\sum_{t=2}^T\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty\le B$.
mu_{t,i}=E_{nu_{t,i}}Y; the entire deterministic mean schedule is fixed before interaction.
The variance $\sigma_{t,i}^2=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{t,i}}Y$ is a deterministic property of the fixed environment.

norms.definition: The ℓ∞ norm measures consecutive differences of the K-dimensional mean vector. It is not a Euclidean norm on action indices.

evidence.supports: Supports the stated results and explicit reductions: $\begin{aligned}[c]\mathcal{R}_T^*&\le C\log(KT)\,\Xi(K,T;Q,B),\\ Q=0:\quad\mathcal{R}_T^*&\le C\Xi(K,T;0,B),\\ \Xi(K,T;Q,B)&=\min\left\{T,\ K+\sqrt{KQ}+(KQBT)^{1/3}\right.\\ &\hspace{7em}\left.+\sqrt{KT}\min\{B,\sqrt B\}\right\}.\end{aligned}$; $\begin{aligned}[c]\mathcal{R}_T^*&\ge c\,\Xi(K,T;Q,B),\\ \Xi(K,T;Q,B)&=\min\left\{T,\ K+\sqrt{KQ}+(KQBT)^{1/3}\right.\\ &\hspace{7em}\left.+\sqrt{KT}\min\{B,\sqrt B\}\right\}.\end{aligned}$. Each bound retains its own model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: The source statements and budget conventions have been checked. This profile uses only the explicitly compatible portions of the linked atomic bounds.
